title: UI interaction tests do not gate ordinary PR CI
impact: Core tests and an app build can be green while cockpit and pane interaction tests never execute.
recommendation: Run the affected UI crate test targets in required PR CI; retain narrow local verification.
acceptance: A deliberate failing cockpit interaction regression fails the required PR check, and restoring it makes that same check green.

title: Some UI tests bypass real keyboard and opener dispatch
impact: Direct handler calls can pass when binding precedence, focus or the visible opener prevents the user reaching that handler.
recommendation: Add real click/key regression paths with production bindings, normal viewport and a populated composer. Keep helper tests but do not count them as entry-point verification.
acceptance: Empty-panel Enter opens its highlighted panel without sending a prompt. Each PR entry point visibly opens its intended target through normal event dispatch.

title: Required-form editability coverage never proves valid typed submission
impact: The negative-only test can pass if typing never edits the required field, because both an invalid value and an untouched empty field are rejected.
recommendation: Type a valid value through the real field, repaint, submit, assert the exact typed answer and unchanged composer.
acceptance: A typed 2 survives repaint and reaches the correct decision as integer 2; invalid 9 produces a visible error and no answer.

title: Default UI checks do not establish native Chromium behavior
impact: Synthetic browser frames and a non-CEF app build cannot prove native page input, focus transfer, navigation or frame delivery.
recommendation: Use a feature-aware native smoke gate for browser changes against a local fixture page and temporary profile.
acceptance: A CEF-enabled app accepts a real page-input click, text and Enter; back/forward change the visible document; host focus returns correctly. Fake-engine tests cannot satisfy this gate.

title: Window geometry still resets at launch
impact: Users must repeatedly resize and reposition Ferrite because launch always supplies centered 1440 by 900 bounds.
recommendation: Persist normal bounds and maximized state, validate restored geometry against attached displays, and use a fitting fallback.
acceptance: Temporary-profile relaunch restores usable size, position and maximization; a disconnected saved monitor never strands the window.

title: Factory schedules do not offer one-time or sub-hour scheduled prompts
impact: Optional T3 parity gap for lightweight reminders or frequent prompts. Ferrite already supports recurring Factory automation and should not be described as lacking scheduling.
recommendation: Make an explicit product decision about lightweight thread scheduling. If adopted, add one-time scheduling and destination selection while preserving missed/overlap policies.
acceptance: An adopted one-time task runs once after restart, shows its destination and result, and does not silently repeat or duplicate an active run.

title: No first-class guest thread participation was found
impact: Optional collaboration gap. No discovered Ferrite entry point lets another person view one thread and propose owner-approved messages.
ferrite_evidence: Repository search over application crates, API/protocol, palette and settings found no guest-share route; absence is bounded and inferred.
recommendation: Prioritize after broken primary workflows. If collaboration is adopted, define read scope, expiry, revocation and owner approval before exposing a share control.
acceptance: If adopted, the guest sees only the intended thread, proposed messages await owner action, and revocation ends access. Otherwise document the deliberate product boundary.

title: T3 device panels have no Ferrite panel counterpart
impact: Optional mobile-development parity gap. Ferrite's panel model has no embedded iOS or Android device tab; external provider device tools remain possible.
recommendation: Treat as a product boundary until current panel/browser interactions are reliable. If adopted, use the existing tab identity and focus model.
acceptance: An adopted device opens one identified tab, repeated opens activate it, device input remains scoped, and disconnect/reconnect is visible without breaking other panel focus.

title: CLI help advertises variadic provider arguments that the parser rejects
impact: Parent reproduced a provider launch failure when following the apparent list syntax. Repeated --args flags work, but help does not make that invocation clear.
recommendation: Print repeatable-list syntax and a provider-argument example in generated help, or explicitly define a trailing passthrough boundary. Correct callers relying on unsupported syntax.
acceptance: The generated thread-start help example parses to args ["--model", "fable", "--effort", "high"] without launching a provider; unknown Ferrite flags retain precise errors.
